theory.title: Passive infinitives and gerunds
theory.explanation: Use to be + past participle after verbs and adjectives that require an infinitive, and being + past participle after prepositions or verbs followed by a gerund: The film needs to be edited; I remember being interviewed.
theory.tip: Passive infinitive: to be + participio. Passive gerund: being + participio.

content.passage: Making a film involves many stages. First, the script needs to be checked and the locations have to be chosen. During production, the actors may dislike being interrupted, so the crew works quietly. After filming, the scenes need to be edited and the sound must be added. Before the premiere, the guests expect to be introduced and the final version is checked once more.

In the future, I think media will become more personalised, but good journalism will remain important.

A: I read a positive review online. B: Was it from a reliable source? A: Yes, although there was one advertisement during the break. B: I watched it on a streaming service. A: What's your opinion of the series? B: It's a very interesting programme.
